correctness.rationale: The unweighted K_{r,r} cut projector kernel is an exact orthogonal ANOVA projection. Rank-one inversion on the mean-zero vertex space gives all conductance-dependent entries with positive denominator. Counting its exceptional-column signs gives rational functions; Rayleigh optimization proves the exact common upper value and distinct weights. Every ordinary cut column is <5 and every ordinary cycle column is <6 uniformly for r>=3, while the exceptional optimum exceeds 6 for r>=29. All quantifiers follow analytically. Standalone exact-rational incidence reconstruction checked 38124 entries; finite computations do not substitute for infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: Published-literature comparisons, topical index searches and inspected primary-paper theorem comparisons found no identical, equivalent or stronger result for sharp sup over one edge conductance of weighted canonical K_{r,r} endpoint projection norms. Earlier static unweighted and deletion cases are not strong enough. Electrical-flow localization works on nonmatching spectral/average norms. Residual bibliographic risk is explicit, and this does not certify absolute historical uniqueness.
residual_risks: Unindexed electrical-network or numerical linear algebra literature might have an equivalent sharp conductance-tuned complete-bipartite endpoint formula.
The first sufficient exact-optimization graph size r=29 is not proved to be the smallest such graph order; no claim is made for smaller orders.
The audit compares relevant primary theorem statements and sections, not every possible historical source.

value.rationale: A single tuned edge in a dense otherwise unit-conductance K_{r,r} raises the canonical endpoint Hodge norms from bounded (<4) to a sharp 3/(2√2) sqrt(r) leading law. The common sharp value, distinct unique conductance optimizers, and their exact product relation are natural operator invariants and expose a meaningful distinction from spectral localization. This is not a routine fixed-parameter evaluation; no claim is made about minimal projection constants.
